text:
alex: heads up — after yesterday's autotuner change i'm seeing a consistent latency spike for tiny prefill requests (1–8 tokens). p95 for prefill went from ~18ms -> ~72ms on A100 pools. :eyes:

maria: ugh. quick question — is this only on prefill or both prefill+decode?

alex: mostly prefill. decode path seems fine. root cause looks like kernel selection choosing a long-seq matmul kernel because batches are padded to the largest seq in the batch (we had a 128-token outlier). autotune mapped that bucket to the long kernel and now tiny prefill ops are routed there.

devin: can you paste the profiler flame or a few numbers?

alex: profiling snippet:```
workload: 30k small prefill requests/hour
before: prefill p95=18ms, p99=34ms, tokens/sec=35k
after:  prefill p95=72ms, p99=140ms, tokens/sec=20k
batching: avg batch size=8, max padded seq=128
kernel chosen: matmul_v2_long (optimized for seq>64)
```

kai: that matches my local repro. autotuner's history window saw the 128 outlier and biased the mapping. two problems: (1) we don't separate prefill vs decode when building buckets, (2) we don't weight by request frequency, so one big outlier flips the bucket mapping.

hannah: on H100 this is worse because the 'long' kernel has higher startup overhead for small AV, so latency amplifies.

maria: proposed mitigation: 1) make bucketing pad-aware per-operation (prefill vs decode) 2) use percentile-based bucketing (e.g., ignore >95th outliers when assigning kernel for a bucket) 3) add an immediate short-term guardrail: cap chosen kernel for prefill to 'seq<=64' if median seq < 32.

devin: +1. can we implement a quick config flag to force pad-aware prefills while we roll a proper autotune change?

alex: i hacked a quick server-side override and numbers look good:```
# runtime config snippet (temporary)
autotune:{
  prefill_bucketing: enabled,
  prefill_buckets: ["1-8","9-32","33-64","65-256"],
  ignore_tail_percentile: 95,
  max_prefill_kernel_seq: 64
}
```

perf-bot: Perf alert created: PF-2026-881 — prefill latency regression detected. Linked traces: https://perf/reports/PF-2026-881

kai: can we also change the heuristic for effective_seq_len = max(user_seq, kv_span) so that cached continuations don't push prefill into long kernels?

hannah: yes — and we should treat kv_span differently between prefill (initial context materialization) and decode (single-step generation). kv_cache warmup should pick a small-kernel warm path.

maria: design notes i want to follow up with: - separate kernel mappings for prefill vs decode - bucket by actual effective_seq distribution (median+90th) - add a decay factor so old outliers don't persist in autotune history - expose a per-deployment soft-cap override (for H100 vs A100 ops)

alex: quick perf delta after the override (A100 test cluster):```
with override: prefill p95=22ms, p99=42ms, tokens/sec=33k
improvement: p95 -50ms vs regression, tokens/sec +65% vs regressed state
```

devin: solid. action items: (1) kai to land short-term runtime flag (pad-aware prefill) by EOD, (2) maria to spec autotune rebalance algorithm that ignores >95th outliers and weights by request freq, (3) hannah to add H100 soft-cap tuning matrix, (4) alex to monitor PF-2026-881 and post dashboards.

kai: i'll do the runtime flag PR and add unit tests for bucket assignment. ping me if you have edge cases — especially mixed-batch scenarios.

maria: i'll draft the autotune spec, including a simulation harness to run synthetic mixes (lots of 2-token queries + occasional long ones).

alex: thanks everyone. i'm going to roll the temp override to prod for the affected A100 pools now. posting follow-up after 30m. :rocket:

perf-bot: Update: PF-2026-881 mitigated via runtime override; monitoring shows prefill p95 back near baseline.```
